headline: Take-Two gets hammered as GTA 6 concerns grow, while Labor's tax-cut-for-CGT-reform deal is the political story of the day.

portfolio.summary: Take-Two was the big mover — down 4.4% on continued GTA 6 jitters. Alphabet slipped 1.2% despite upbeat earnings coverage, likely profit-taking after a strong run. The ASX-listed ETFs were mostly green, with VGE (emerging markets) the standout gainer at +1.2%. CBA gave back a touch. MSFT and FUEL barely moved.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Ongoing GTA 6 concerns — questions about budget blowout and scale weighing on sentiment. Down over 4%.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Dipped despite positive earnings coverage and Gemini Omni launch. Looks like some post-earnings profit-taking.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Best performer in the portfolio today — EM getting a lift as AUD/USD firms and risk appetite holds.

movers.name: Commonwealth Bank of Australia
movers.note: Small pullback, likely reflecting softening RBA rate hike expectations reducing bank margin outlook.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: Modest gain tracking a broadly positive S&P 500 session.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Steady gains consistent with broad market lift across global equities.

markets.summary: Markets broadly positive overnight. The S&P 500 and ASX 200 both edged higher, with no major catalysts — more of a calm drift upward. Gold is barely budging near $4,523. WTI crude held flat at $96.60. The AUD pushed up to 0.7173, its strongest level in recent sessions, driven by factors other than RBA rate hike expectations (which are actually softening).

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Steady grind higher — markets shrugging off macro noise.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Modest gain; bond demand returning as rate hike bets unwind.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech soft relative to broader market — some rotation away from mega-caps.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Flat; US-Iran deal hopes have added supply-side pressure, keeping lid on prices.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Essentially unchanged — holding near record highs.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: AUD rising despite RBA rate hike odds falling — worth watching.

politics.summary: Two big domestic stories today: Labor is playing hardball by tying popular tax cuts to CGT and negative gearing reforms — a bold political move that will fire up the property debate. Separately, RBA rate hike expectations are unwinding fast, which is why bond demand is picking up and the AUD is behaving oddly. The firearms cap rejection by Victorian Premier Allan is a state-level story with limited national legs.

stories.title: Labor to tie tax cuts to CGT and negative gearing changes
stories.why_it_matters: This is a significant political gambit. Labor is using popular income tax cuts as leverage to push through property tax reform. If it sticks, it could meaningfully affect investment property economics — relevant if you hold property or property-adjacent stocks.

stories.title: RBA interest rate rise bets unwind, triggering demand for Australian bonds
stories.why_it_matters: Rate hike bets unwinding is good news for growth stocks and bond holders, but it may squeeze bank margins further — one reason CBA softened today.

stories.title: Why is the Australian Dollar rising despite weakening RBA rate hike odds?
stories.why_it_matters: A stronger AUD reduces the AUD-hedged returns on your US-listed holdings (GOOGL, MSFT, TTWO). Worth keeping an eye on if the move continues.

stories.title: Temporary fall in inflation won't ease RBA fears
stories.why_it_matters: Counterpoint to the rate-cut narrative — the RBA may not be done yet. Mixed signals mean uncertainty remains for rate-sensitive stocks.

ai.summary: Today's AI news is dominated by a single theme: Pope Leo XIV's first encyclical calling for robust global AI regulation — a rare moment of moral authority entering the AI governance debate. The other story worth noting is Google's launch of Gemini Omni, a new flagship multimodal model that matters directly for your GOOGL holding.

stories.title: Introducing Gemini Omni
stories.why_it_matters: Google's latest flagship multimodal AI model. Alphabet needs to keep pace with OpenAI and Anthropic — this is a signal they're still competing hard. Positive for GOOGL long-term.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV urges robust AI regulation in encyclical — warns some weapons now beyond human control
stories.why_it_matters: The Vatican entering the AI governance debate gives political cover for regulators globally to move faster on AI oversight. Could accelerate legislation in the EU and elsewhere — a headwind for AI companies long-term, though likely slow-moving.

stories.title: Pope calls for robust AI regulation — warns of risks in finance and warfare
stories.why_it_matters: The encyclical specifically calls out AI risks in financial markets and autonomous weapons — two domains where regulatory risk for tech companies is real. More background than immediate market-mover.

sport.summary: AFL is the dominant story with the passing of Neale Daniher — a genuine legend of the game. On the NRL front, Round 13 team lists are taking shape with injury clouds over several clubs. A WSL surf event in NZ has been suspended after an Aussie photographer was bitten by what may have been a shark.

stories.title: Neale Daniher, football legend and Fight MND campaigner, dies aged 65
stories.why_it_matters: One of the most respected figures in Australian sport. Daniher's Fight MND campaign raised tens of millions and changed the conversation around the disease. The AFL world is mourning today.

stories.title: NRL Round 13 predicted teams: Mystery surrounds Origin stars; Tigers and Warriors cop major injury blows
stories.why_it_matters: With State of Origin selection drama and injury concerns at multiple clubs, Round 13 team lists are far from settled. Worth tracking if you follow NRL Fantasy or have a team in the mix.

stories.title: World Surf League event in NZ put on hold after Australian photographer bitten by 'shark or sea lion'
stories.why_it_matters: WSL event suspended in NZ — unusual incident. Worth watching if the event is rescheduled, especially given Gold Coast's surf scene.

stories.title: AFL Round 12 Review: Team stuns with 20-minute blitz
stories.why_it_matters: Round 12 wrap — catch up on the results before Round 13 hits this week.

watch_today.title: Take-Two (TTWO) — down 4.4%, GTA 6 risk building
watch_today.detail: TTWO has now had a meaningful pullback on concerns that GTA 6 is overscoped and potentially delayed. No confirmed release date shift yet, but sentiment is souring. Review your position sizing if you're overweight.

watch_today.title: Labor's CGT / negative gearing reform gambit
watch_today.detail: Labor is linking income tax cuts to capital gains and negative gearing changes. If this gains traction, it could reshape investment property economics in Australia. Watch for reaction from the opposition and property lobby this week.

watch_today.title: AUD/USD rising despite RBA rate cut bets — unusual divergence
watch_today.detail: AUD pushing above 0.717 even as RBA hike expectations fall. This compresses unhedged returns on your US holdings. If the AUD continues to strengthen, USD-denominated gains (GOOGL, MSFT, TTWO) shrink when converted back.

watch_today.title: Google launches Gemini Omni — positive signal for GOOGL
watch_today.detail: New flagship multimodal model shows Google is still competing at the frontier. No immediate share price catalyst, but reinforces the AI growth thesis for Alphabet.
